title: Qcqs higher direct images preserve a fixed set of torsion primes
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal P$ be any set of primes and let $F\in\Ab(U_{\Et})$ be an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and every $x\in F_{\bar u}$ there is a positive integer $n$ with $nx=0$ and with every prime divisor of $n$ in $\mathcal P$. Then for every integer $q\geq0$, every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, and every $y\in(R^qu_*F)_{\bar v}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], there is a positive integer $m$ with $my=0$ and with every prime divisor of $m$ in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 0DDD, lemma-torsion-direct-image (1), with the fixed-prime refinement of the proof of Tag 0DDC, lemma-torsion-cohomology (1): restrict annihilators to integers with prime divisors in P.

proof.text: Fix a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar v$ with $W$ affine, and put $Z=U\times_VW$, with projection $a:Z\to U$. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $Z\to W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] therefore makes the scheme $Z$ qcqs. Set $G=a^{-1}F$. For every geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies $G_{\bar z}$ with $F_{a\bar z}$, so every element of $G_{\bar z}$ has an annihilator with the prescribed prime divisors. This uses no global qcqs hypothesis on $U$ or $V$.

source.place: Tag 0DDD, lemma-torsion-direct-image (1), affine test object; Schemes Tags 01K5, 01KU(4), 01K4 and 01KN; pullback stalk formula

proof.text: Let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime divisors belong to $\mathcal P$, ordered by divisibility. It is a small nonempty directed partial order: $1$ belongs to it and $nm$ is a common upper bound of $n,m$. For $n\in S_{\mathcal P}$ define $G[n]=\ker(n:G\to G)$ using [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]. If $n\mid m$, a section killed by $n$ is killed by $m$, so the inclusions form a diagram and a cocone to $G$. Form its sheaf colimit $C$ using [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], and let $c:C\to G$ be the induced map. The index set is a subset of the natural numbers, hence fits the coefficient universe required by directed cohomology continuity.

source.place: Tag 0DDC, lemma-torsion-cohomology (1), restricted annihilator index; Modules on Sites Tag 03CO(1),(2),(4)

proof.text: We prove that the cocone just constructed is colimiting with vertex $G$, rather than invoking the unrestricted torsion union. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], $(G[n])_{\bar z}=\ker(n:G_{\bar z}\to G_{\bar z})$. By [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], $C_{\bar z}$ is the colimit of these subgroups. Every element of $G_{\bar z}$ belongs to one of them by step 1. To check injectivity of $c_{\bar z}$, represent an element of $C_{\bar z}$ by $x\in(G[n])_{\bar z}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with $R=\mathbf Z$ (abelian groups have their canonical $\mathbf Z$-module structure). If its image in $G_{\bar z}$ is zero, $x=0$ because this is a subgroup inclusion, so its colimit class is zero. Thus $c_{\bar z}$ is bijective at every geometric point. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes $c$ an isomorphism. Its composites with the colimit legs are exactly the inclusions $G[n]\to G$, so these inclusions exhibit $G$ as their colimit.

source.place: Tag 0DDC, lemma-torsion-cohomology (1), fixed-prime union justified on stalks; Tag 03PT(3),(4), theorem-exactness-stalks; Algebra Tag 00D6

proof.text:
The scheme $Z$ is qcqs and $S_{\mathcal P}$ is a small nonempty directed partial order. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-directed-cohomology-colimit] to the diagram $n\mapsto G[n]$ and the colimit cocone of step 3. It gives
$$H^q(Z_{\Et},G)=\varinjlim_{n\in S_{\mathcal P}}H^q(Z_{\Et},G[n]),$$
with coprojections induced by the actual inclusions $G[n]\hookrightarrow G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with $R=\mathbf Z$, any class $b\in H^q(Z_{\Et},G)$ is the image of a class $b_n\in H^q(Z_{\Et},G[n])$ for some $n\in S_{\mathcal P}$. There is no uniform annihilator assumption on $G$, and no torsion assumption is needed for this continuity theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DDC, lemma-torsion-cohomology (1); Tag 03Q5, lemma-colimit; Algebra Tag 00D6

proof.text:
The sectionwise kernel description in [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel] gives $n\operatorname{id}_{G[n]}=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](2), $H^q(Z_{\Et},-)$ is $R^q\Gamma(Z,-)$ for the left exact additive sections functor. [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] says that these derived functors form a delta functor, whose degree functors are additive. Consequently
$$n\operatorname{id}_{H^q(Z_{\Et},G[n])}=H^q(n\operatorname{id}_{G[n]})=H^q(0)=0.$$
Indeed an additive functor sends the sum of $n$ identity maps to the sum of their images, sends the identity to the identity, and sends zero to zero. Thus $nb_n=0$. The coprojection of step 4 is a group homomorphism, so $nb=0$ as well. Every class over the affine neighbourhood $W$ is therefore killed by an integer in $S_{\mathcal P}$.

source.place: Tag 0DDC, lemma-torsion-cohomology (1), final sentence; Derived Categories Tags 015B(4), 05TE, Homology Definition 010Q

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $R^qu_*F$ is the sheafification of the abelian presheaf $W\mapsto H^q(U\times_VW,F|_{U\times_VW})$. [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk] identifies its stalk at $\bar v$ with the presheaf stalk. Pointed etale neighbourhoods form a cofiltered category by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]; their opposite is the filtered index in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The elementwise colimit statement of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], again with $R=\mathbf Z$, therefore represents the given $y$ by a class over some pointed neighbourhood $(W_0,\bar w_0)$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] with the open subset $W_0$ itself to obtain an affine pointed neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(W_0,\bar w_0)$. Restrict the representative to $W$; it has the same stalk class. All stalk index categories are taken in a common universe containing the site and its chosen geometric point, or in a small equivalent category; the colimit assertions are small-index assertions in that universe.

source.place: Tag 0DDD, lemma-torsion-direct-image (1); Tag 03Q8, lemma-higher-direct-images; Tag 03PT(2); Tag 03PQ and affine shrinking in Tag 04HX

proof.text: Apply steps 1--5 to the affine representative $b$ obtained in step 6. There is $m\in S_{\mathcal P}$ with $mb=0$. The canonical map from its cohomology group into the stalk is a group homomorphism and takes $b$ to $y$, hence $my=0$. By definition of $S_{\mathcal P}$, $m>0$ and every prime divisor of $m$ belongs to $\mathcal P$. This proves the assertion for arbitrary $q\ge0$ and arbitrary $\bar v$.
